subject: Planned deprecation of inference-rf-v1 — timeline, exceptions, and comms
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Planned deprecation of inference-rf-v1 — proposed timeline & asks

Team —

Quick sync: Product wants to start a formal deprecation for the older model variant inference-rf-v1 (the non-quantized baseline). Goal is to move traffic to inference-rf-2.0 (primary replacement) and keep rf-compat as a short-term compatibility shim.

Proposed high-level timeline: 
- 2027-06-15: Deprecation freeze for hosted (stop new signups pinned to rf-v1)
- 2027-07-01: Public announcement to customers (90-day migration window)
- 2027-10-01: Sunsetting of rf-v1 on hosted (final cutover; dedicated/private require separate signoff)

Primary asks: 
- Engineering (karthik, marcus): confirm infra/compat risks and estimate any forced migration work (SDK hooks, kernel fallbacks, routing)
- Docs/Comms (hannah, lauren): draft customer-facing comms and dev notice; outline rollback messaging and migration steps
- Sales (priyom): identify enterprise customers that should get earlier notice or an exceptions path

Attachments: deprecation_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook draft), migration_checklist.xlsx (customer checklist). Also see infra_impact_notes.docx referenced below.

Please reply with: (1) any required changes to dates (2) the list of customers who need >90 days, and (3) owners for the items in the playbook. I need alignment by end of week (2027-04-15) so we can lock the announcement cadence.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned deprecation of inference-rf-v1 — proposed timeline & asks

Monica + team —

Thanks for the draft. A few infra notes from my side after a quick review of the runtime and kernel compatibility surface: 
- rf-v1 uses a legacy attention kernel path that rf-2.0 replaces. We can provide an rf-compat runtime but it will carry ~12-18% higher p99 latency at large seq lengths.
- For hosted customers the timeline you propose is OK, but for Dedicated capacity customers (reserved pools) we need additional lead time to coordinate node reimages and capacity shading. Recommend moving the freeze for Dedicated to 2027-06-01 (so it’s earlier than hosted freeze) to avoid capacity crunch during the public announcement window.
- Engineering tasks I expect: QA for KV cache migration, canary config in two regions, and an automated smoke test that validates inference outputs for 50 canonical prompts.

I attached infra_impact_notes.docx with granular rollout risks and a proposed canary checklist. I strongly recommend we add a short "performance impact" section to customer comms so we set expectations.

If Product accepts the Dedicated change, I can own the infra rollout and scheduling with SRE.

—Marcus
Director, Serving Infrastructure

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned deprecation of inference-rf-v1 — proposed timeline & asks

Agree with Marcus on the infra asks. A couple of engineering items to call out explicitly: 
1) SDK compatibility shim — we need ~3 weeks to add a compatibility flag that auto-maps rf-v1 calls to rf-compat when customers haven't migrated. The shim should be opt-out.
2) Migration tool — one-time tool to rewrite pinned model references in customer configs (applies to Dedicated/Private). Estimate: 2 engineers for 3 sprints to build and test.
3) Exceptions gating — propose the following criteria for an exemption: 
   - Legal/regulatory constraints (data residency, audit)
   - Private/on-prem or air-gapped installs where upgrade requires on-site work
   - Reserved Dedicated customers with contractual upgrade windows

For exemptions, we need a formal request template and an engineering review SLA (recommended 10 business days). I can own the review SLA and technical validation checks.

Also: fallback policy should prefer routing to rf-compat with a clear log entry and an opt-in for aggressive fallback to rf-2.0 only if the customer has confirmed compatibility.

Karthik
VP, Engineering — Serving Runtime
